presidency/what-is-cop.title: What is COP? What is COP32?
presidency/what-is-cop.summary: The world's highest-level annual climate negotiation, and why COP32 matters for Africa.

sections.heading: What is COP?
body: The Conference of the Parties, or COP, is the supreme decision-making body of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), adopted in 1992. Each year, nearly every nation on earth meets to review implementation of the Convention and decide on the collective response to climate change.

COP is the leading multilateral forum for global climate governance — the venue where emission targets are negotiated, finance is mobilised, and collective action advances from one session to the next.

sections.heading: The Role of COP in Global Climate Governance
body: At the centre of each session is a review of Parties' national communications and greenhouse gas inventories, assessed against the overall goals of the Convention.

list.body: Reviewing what countries are actually doing against their commitments.

list.title: Progress toward the Convention's objective
list.body: Tracking collective progress against the 1.5°C pathway.

list.title: Raising ambition and implementation
list.body: Identifying where targets and delivery need to go further.

sections.heading: What is COP32?
body: COP32 is the 32nd session of the Conference of the Parties, hosted by Ethiopia in Addis Ababa in 2027. The session continues the process begun at COP30 in Belém and COP31 in Antalya, advancing dialogue, consensus, and — above all — implementation.

As host, Ethiopia brings the perspective of a continent on the front line of climate impacts, and a seat of African diplomacy as home to both the African Union and the UN Economic Commission for Africa.

list.title: Emission Targets & Implementation
list.body: Strengthened Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement.

list.title: Climate Finance
list.body: Delivering against the new collective quantified finance goal set at COP29.

list.title: Adaptation & Resilience
list.body: Protecting the most vulnerable countries and communities from climate impacts.

sections.heading: Why Ethiopia, Why Addis Ababa?
body: Ethiopia sits at the heart of the Horn of Africa, a region acutely exposed to drought and climate variability, and has invested heavily in renewable energy and reforestation through its Green Legacy Initiative. Addis Ababa's standing as Africa's diplomatic capital makes it a natural home for a COP focused on turning global commitments into action for the continent.

sections.heading: Leadership
body: Ethiopia's COP32 Presidency is led by a President-Designate, supported by a National Organising Committee that brings together government ministries, the City Administration of Addis Ababa, and technical experts seconded from the UNFCCC Secretariat.

The Presidency works in close coordination with the African Union and the UN Economic Commission for Africa, both headquartered in Addis Ababa, to ensure the continent's priorities are reflected throughout the negotiations.

vision/success.title: Vision for Success
vision/success.summary: COP32: a turning point for climate action, built on dialogue, consensus, and delivery.

sections.heading: A Turning Point for Climate Action
body: COP32 aims to be remembered not for the pledges it produced, but for what was actually delivered. Addis Ababa becomes a working table where governments, cities, business, and civil society convert years of negotiation into financed, measurable projects.

That shift starts with trust. Rebuilding confidence between developed and developing nations — and between negotiators and the communities they represent — is the foundation every other outcome at COP32 depends on.

pillars.title: Rebuilding Trust Through Dialogue
pillars.body: Giving a real seat at the table to vulnerable nations, local governments, civil society, and youth — not just national delegations.

pillars.title: Shared Responsibility Through Consensus
pillars.body: Treating energy security and emissions goals as complementary, and building consensus around a transition that is fair to workers and economies alike.

pillars.title: Turning Commitments Into Action
pillars.body: Linking global targets to funded, on-the-ground projects through an expanded Climate Implementation Bridge.

vision/climate-story.title: Ethiopia's Climate Story
vision/climate-story.summary: A nation that has planted its way into the global climate conversation.

sections.heading: Ethiopia's Climate Story
body: Ethiopia adopted its Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) Strategy in 2011, one of the earliest national plans to pursue economic growth without increasing emissions — a framework that still guides the country's climate policy today.

Since 2019, the Green Legacy Initiative has mobilised millions of citizens each rainy season in nationwide tree-planting campaigns, restoring degraded land and raising public awareness of climate action at a scale few countries have matched.
Hosting COP32 builds on this record, and on Ethiopia's long-standing role as a seat of African diplomacy, as home to both the African Union and the UN Economic Commission for Africa.

sections.heading: Climate Cooperation
body: As host to the African Union and the UN Economic Commission for Africa, Addis Ababa is already a hub for continental climate diplomacy, from the Africa Climate Summit process to regional adaptation initiatives.
COP32 strengthens this role, deepening South-South cooperation and linking African priorities — adaptation finance, debt, and just transition — directly into the global negotiations.

conference/overview.title: Conference Overview
conference/overview.summary: What to expect from the two-week COP32 conference in Addis Ababa.

sections.heading: Conference Overview
body: COP32 runs for two weeks in Addis Ababa, combining formal UNFCCC negotiations with a public-facing programme of events, exhibitions, and side events across the Blue and Green Zones.

The first week focuses on technical negotiations between national delegations; the second week brings in Ministers and Heads of State for the high-level segment where final political decisions are made.

facts.value: Blue Zone negotiations + Green Zone public programme

conference/overview.note: Exact conference dates will be confirmed by the UNFCCC Secretariat closer to 2027.

sections.heading: COP32 Venue
body: The UN Conference Centre Addis Ababa (UNCC-AA) is a purpose-built United Nations facility, home to the UN Economic Commission for Africa and a regular venue for African Union summits and major international gatherings.
Its scale and existing UN security and logistics infrastructure make it a natural home for the Blue Zone negotiations, with surrounding grounds adapted to host the Green Zone's public programme.

Green Zone registration, coordinated by the COP32 Presidency, is open to the private sector, academia, civil society, and members of the public, with capacity-limited free and ticketed sessions.

sections.heading: Flight Ticket
body: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport is Ethiopian Airlines' home hub and one of Africa's busiest gateways, with direct connections to major cities across Africa, Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
Delegates and attendees are encouraged to book flights early, as hosting a UN conference of this scale typically drives strong demand on routes into Addis Ababa during the conference period.

faq.q: Do I need a visa to attend COP32?
faq.a: Most nationalities will need an e-Visa or visa on arrival — requirements vary by passport, so check before you travel.
E-Visa applications are typically processed within a few working days when submitted online.
Standard e-Visa fees apply. Any conference-specific arrangements will be announced by the Presidency closer to the date.

faq.q: What if my passport details change after I apply?
faq.a: Contact e-Visa support through the official portal to update your application.

visitor/visa.note: Entry requirements vary by nationality — always confirm current rules with an official Ethiopian government or embassy source before travelling.

visitor/plan-your-travel.title: Plan Your Travel
visitor/plan-your-travel.summary: Practical notes for visiting Addis Ababa.

sections.heading: Plan Your Travel
body: Addis Ababa sits at roughly 2,355 metres above sea level, with a mild, spring-like climate year-round — pack layers, as evenings are noticeably cooler than the daytime.
The local currency is the Ethiopian Birr (ETB). Credit card acceptance is improving but remains limited outside major hotels, so carrying some local currency is recommended.
